messages:
An instrument archives records in one continuous wire string. Deliver its byte map as a JSON artifact. Submit either the JSON object inline or one Markdown download link to the checked JSON file; the recipient uses exactly those bytes.

The ordered records are (JSON escapes denote their usual characters):
[{"tag": "μ", "text": "n\t"}, {"tag": "Q\\\"", "text": "雪"}, {"tag": "e", "text": "é"}, {"tag": "E", "text": "🪁\r\n"}, {"tag": "/", "text": ""}, {"tag": "μ", "text": "Ω"}]

For each record append tag, a literal colon, text, and one U+001E record separator, in that order. No other delimiter, padding, normalization or terminal newline. Index the concatenation in UTF-8 bytes, starting at zero. In packet.payloads report each record index and the half-open byte span of its text only (even for empty text). A read returns record indices in input order whose text spans have positive byte overlap with its half-open window. An empty span or window cannot have positive overlap. Reads may bisect a UTF-8 character.

Evaluate the following (lo,hi) windows in order: [[0, 3], [3, 7], [8, 12], [16, 17], [17, 17], [21, 24]].

Supply a further nonempty integer window, within the wire, different from all six requested windows. Its strict read must hit at least one record. Demonstrate it distinguishes the correct test max(lo,begin) < min(hi,end) from the faulty <= test applied mechanically even to empty spans. Return both arrays for that exact window.

Exact output shape (the numbers, arrays and strings below illustrate field types only):
{"packet":{"wire":"…","payloads":[{"record":0,"begin":1,"end":3}],"reads":[[0]]},"proof":{"input":{"window":[0,2]},"strict":[0],"inclusive":[0,1]}}

The recipient expects a decoded wire string, zero-based integer record IDs including repeats of the same tag, and exactly the named fields.
